newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish inflation to end '97 below 2.5 percent-BCH.
newsitem.headline: Spanish inflation to end '97 below 2.5 percent-BCH.

text.p: Spain's Banco Central Hispano forecast a further decline in the country's inflation rate to below 2.5 percent at the end of the year.

"In January, both the general consumer price index and the core index could show a further reduction and the year-on-year rise could end up below the three percent barrier. The downtrend should last during the year and the rate could end below 2.5 percent," the bank said on Wednesday in a study.
BCH added that Spain could meet the European Union convergence criteria at the beginning of 1998 and that a likely average for 1997 inflation would be around 2.8 percent.
Public forecasts put Spain's consumer price inflation at 2.6 percent year-on-year at the end of 1997, while the Bank of Spain's target is for inflation to end the year around 2.5 percent.
